notes: Upstream entrypoint (/entrypoint.sh) executes `chown` and `su-exec node` which requires initial root privileges to drop down to UID 1000. When running under Kubernetes with a non-root security context (e.g. runAsNonRoot: true or runAsUser: 10001), the container will fail with 'su-exec: setgroups: Operation not permitted'. To run safely as non-root, override the container command directly to ['node', 'custom-server.js'] and configure securityContext.fsGroup to grant write access to /app/data.

tunables.label: Server Port
tunables.description: HTTP port used by the upstream Node server.
tunables.troubleshooting: Probes fail after a change unless the compose mapping (20128:20128) and the healthcheck URL are updated to match.

tunables.label: Bind Address
tunables.description: Address on which the upstream server listens.
tunables.troubleshooting: Must be 0.0.0.0 in a container; a loopback bind makes the published port unreachable from the host.

tunables.label: Data Directory
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep it on the declared /app/data volume (the image symlinks ~/.9router to it), otherwise providers, combos and API keys are lost on recreate.

tunables.label: Node Environment
tunables.troubleshooting: Leave at production — development mode exposes verbose errors and disables optimizations.

tunables.label: Disable Telemetry
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep true in containers to avoid outbound telemetry calls; Next.js only honours the value at build/start time, so restart the container after changing it.

tunables.label: Require API Key
tunables.description: Enforce Bearer API key validation on /v1/* routes.
tunables.troubleshooting: Leave false only on loopback — with the default false anyone who can reach port 20128 can drive your connected providers. Keys are created in Dashboard → API Keys and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; a 401 there means REQUIRE_API_KEY is on and the key is missing or wrong.

tunables.label: JWT Secret
tunables.description: Cryptographic secret for signing session cookies (auto-generated in DATA_DIR if unset).
tunables.troubleshooting: Setting it lets several instances share sessions; rotating it logs every dashboard session out. If logins fail right after a volume wipe, the auto-generated secret changed — either re-login or pin this value. The example is a local-only placeholder.

tunables.label: API Key Secret
tunables.description: HMAC secret for validating generated API keys.
tunables.troubleshooting: Upstream ships an obvious default — change it before exposing the instance, because a predictable secret lets anyone mint accepted keys. Keep it stable afterwards or previously issued keys stop validating.

tunables.label: Initial Admin Password
tunables.description: First-time admin login password on initial setup.
tunables.troubleshooting: Upstream falls back to `123456` when unset — always set your own before publishing the port, then change it in the dashboard after the first login. It is ignored once a saved hash exists.

tunables.label: CORS Origin
tunables.description: Allowed origin header for web dashboard API callers.
tunables.troubleshooting: Not part of 9router's upstream `.env` contract — the documented knobs are AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE and REQUIRE_API_KEY — so verify with `docker exec <c> env` plus browser devtools whether the header is actually emitted. If it is not, enforce origin/CORS policy in the reverse proxy instead of relying on this variable.

tunables.label: Internal Base URL
tunables.description: Internal base URL for server-side requests and sync.
tunables.troubleshooting: Build it from the published scheme + host + PORT (include the reverse-proxy path when one is in front). A value that resolves to another host makes internal sync/API callbacks time out or hit the wrong service while the dashboard itself still works. NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is the browser-facing counterpart — keep the two consistent or generated links and server-side calls disagree.

tunables.label: Enable Request Logs
tunables.description: Write request/response diagnostic logs under logs/.
tunables.troubleshooting: Turn on temporarily to diagnose 401/404 routing issues, then set it back to false — a busy gateway writes a line per request and the log grows quickly. Changes apply on container restart; confirm output with `docker logs <c>`.
